newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIANS KEEP FAITH AFTER CYPRUS DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIANS KEEP FAITH AFTER CYPRUS DRAW.

text.p: Russia, held to a 1-1 draw by unfancied Cyprus in a World Cup qualifier, will keep faith with their squad, deputy trainer Yuri Syomin said on Monday.
"It was the sort of slip that happens to every team," Syomin said. "We're not going to make some sort of tragedy of it.
"We're keeping our eyes on the future. We still have a good chance of finishing first."
Saturday's result in Cyprus left Russia leading group five by one point from Israel but with Bulgaria, whom Russia play twice this summer, lurking two points behind with a game in hand.

Syomin refused to criticise his Italy-based striking partnership of Igor Kolyvanov and Igor Simutenkov. Reggiana's Simutenkov scored the equaliser after Sinica Gogic gave the injury-hit home side a shock lead in the 31st minute.
But midfielder Alexander Mostovoy's point-blank miss in the dying seconds summed up the Russians' night.
"The team selection was fine," Syomin said.
The absence of Anatoly Kanishchev, who disappeared before the squad left for Cyprus, may have made some difference, he said.
The Alania Vladikavkaz striker resurfaced at the weekend and insisted he had told the squad doctor he was injured.
Kanishchev told the Sport-Express newspaper he visited his family in southern Russia and could not telephone the squad in Cyprus.
